answer.market_read: We are #2 in class (1.599 vs inextro 1.659). The shop is weakest on book (rank 9/53, 194M) and stars (25/53), while revenue is strong (6/53). Revenue is high but profit is thin (33M on 1.56B), so the gain is in margin per unit, not more volume. Big-ticket sofas and beds carry the margin: Jakomo Mate 349k/unit (36M/24h), Avenuel 232k (33.7M), Lacloud 205k (22.8M), Simmons Beautyrest 165k (21.8M). Most stock turns almost instantly (avg_hold about 0h), but Avenuel (24 units, oldest 6.5h, sales slowing from about 36 to 25 per 6h), Simmons (27 units, 77 walkaways) and Zinus Ultima Q (7 units, 3 sold, 22 walkaways) are sitting and losing buyers on price. Some items run out while buyers still ask for them: apples (33 sold-out asks, but cost_surge 1.106 because the whole market is buying), buffalo wings (7), nuts (6), and the low-competition niches Bedrium folding mattress, Zinus Cloud Q and the Jakomo recliner. Those niches have only 2-3 shops and stock at 0-4. Jakomo Mate's cost is surging (1.118, 80 units/h market-wide), so it should be priced up, not bought more of. Zinus Green Tea is a crowded 22-shop commodity with a 36k margin, so there is no room to cut its price; hold it.

playbook: Book is our weakest shop axis: favor margin per unit over raw volume, since revenue rank is already strong.
When cost_surge > 1.08, the market is crowding the SKU: raise the ask instead of raising cover.
Sold-out asks on a SKU with no cost surge and few shops (2-3) means raise cover by 0.5.
Old stock (oldest_h > 4) plus walkaways much higher than sold means cut the ask 3-5%, but only where margin per unit stays above about 10%.
Crowded commodity SKUs (15+ shops, margin under 10%) should not get price cuts; hold the ask and cover.
Big-ticket sofas and beds carry the margin; keep them stocked before chasing cheap high-volume items.
Perishable food: only add cover where hold time is about 0h and sold-out asks are recurring.
Predict sold_next_6h at about 70-85% of the last 6h to absorb noise; use margin predictions only for SKUs that sell steadily.
